newsitem.title: UK: Macfarlane says wage data prodded latest rate cut.
newsitem.headline: Macfarlane says wage data prodded latest rate cut.

text.p: Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) governor Ian Macfarlane said on Thursday that recent wage data had prodded the RBA to cut its overnight cash rates to 5.5 percent from six percent on May 23.

Asked at a bank seminar in London why the central bank had waited to cut rates from its May 6 board meeting, he said, "The crucial variable that changed over that period is we got several figures on wages."
He said details from the figures, and data from the private sector, had told the central bank the situation was better than previously thought.
Australian financial markets were surprised by the cut on May 23 as Macfarlane had previously said wage data had been a setback to last year's pattern of improving developments.
Macfarlane said wage growth of four percent was consistent with the country's inflation goal.
"Then, when we added to this clear indication inflation expectations are coming down...we think it made a pretty convincing case for another easing," he said.
He said the bank had spent a fair amount of time agonising over what was happening over wages.
He said it was difficult to glean a picture of the wages situation in Australia because it was in a process of transition from a centralised system to a decentralised system.
Some sectors of the economy had their wages determined by bargaining, and some through a reward system. He said it was important to get an idea of the average.
"This came out last month and showed they are growing in our estimation by four percent...and this appears to be consistent with the inflation target."
